chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the pools in which urine is passed. He said: “There is no harm, if the color of the water overcomes the color of the urine.”
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: The proper way to understand this report is when the water in it is more than a kurr, as we have explained.

key_terms.الْخَبَرِ: the report or hadith being interpreted
key_terms.كُرٍّ: a legally significant large measure of water in ritual purity rulings
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal problem
key_terms.لَوْنُ الْمَاءِ: the color of the water, indicating its dominant state

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on pool water if urine falls into it in Shi'a fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on pools into which urine has entered. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that there is no problem when the water remains dominant over the urine, and Shaykh al-Ṭūsī clarifies that this is understood in the case of water amounting to more than a kurr. The report is significant in discussions of ritual purity and the legal rulings of water.
